research_question: Can cost-matched counterfactual variant supervision reduce evidence-reference instability under relevant and irrelevant visible changes?
development_observation: ordinary SFT confirmation errors include programs that switch references across variants after prompt-visible scoring correction

training.base_tasks: the same exact 512 task_ids used by the v2 ordinary/visible LoRA SFT arms
training.control_arm: duplicate_original_control_sft: each original prompt/target row appears twice
training.candidate_arm: paired_variant_stability_sft: each task contributes one original row and one deterministic relevant or irrelevant variant row with the same target program
training.fairness: same tasks, targets, steps, optimizer, sequence cap and batch schedule; candidate sees more prompt surface variation and the control matches row count/exposure

confirmation.source_boundary: same-source TAT-QA new table families, not a new benchmark family
confirmation.selection: stable SHA-256 task-id order, first 24 remaining train-split tasks with unique table_uid

metrics.primary: paired program correctness across all three variants

decision_rule.continue_candidate: paired arm improves paired completion by >=10 percentage points over both cost-matched control and ordinary SFT, with table-cluster bootstrap interval lower bound >0 against the stronger comparator
decision_rule.stop_candidate: otherwise stop this stability-supervision candidate and retain the residual as a bounded reference-selection problem
